pr_title: Optimize the initialization of the OrdinalCasing::s_sCasingTable table.
pr_body:
The table was initialized in the .cctor and it contains a large amount of object references, so the generated cctor was
1K IL. Replace with a byte table and a loop.

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/43732.

issue_context.title: Large memory dependency in OrdinalCasing::ToUpper
issue_context.body: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/43bc8e85d16db7a5a152bea86a55b492027bf420/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/OrdinalCasing.Icu.cs#L88 has a dependency on the large array which is unnecessary. The whole array is about ~25k~ 2k and aggressively allocated in the static constructor but it needs to actually store only 32 bytes of data. Please replaced the multi-dimensional array with simple binary map (0 for existing null, 1 for s_noCasingPage).
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Tagging subscribers to this area: @tarekgh, @safern, @krwq
See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.

> Please replaced the multi-dimensional array with simple binary map (0 for existing null, 1 for s_noCasingPage).

This is not going to work, at runtime we allocate more dynamic tables and add to this static array.

> This is not true. the whole static array size is 256 * sizeof(IntPtr) which maximum static allocation is 2K

Sorry, that was a typo, it's 2k which is still very large.

> This is not going to work, at runtime we allocate more dynamic tables and add to this static array.

The existing code only replaces the null entries. I made one suggestion and there are other solutions to remove the large initialization dependency (about 1k of IL) in the code.

review_comments: Couldn't we start i at 16? The first 2 table init entries are `0b00000000`, I wonder if that can change? @tarekgh @GrabYourPitchforks ?

TBH not sure if I'd optimize that away. True, iterating over everything does a little more work than needed, but we're only talking a small handful of unnecessary iterations, and this is a bit more future-proof. It's less likely to incur bugs should we ever need to change the early values.
Yep, that's what I wanted to know if these could actually change in the future, if it can or we're not sure, it makes sense to make it future-proof and iterate over everything.
would be better to keep this table inside a comment. for easier reading and debugging.
